html:
The visit of the Ming treasure fleet of Zheng He to Malindi, a Swahili town on the coast of what is now Kenya, during the fifth voyage of 1417 to 1419. It was among the farthest points the Chinese fleets reached.

Malindi was one of the Swahili city-states that traded across the Indian Ocean. In 1415 its envoys had brought a giraffe to the Yongle Emperor in Nanjing. Courtiers hailed it as a qilin, a creature of good omen, which flattered the emperor. The fleet then carried the envoys home and visited Mogadishu and other ports of the coast.

The voyages showed the reach of early Ming China, but they were costly and ended in 1433. Eighty years later, in 1498, Vasco da Gama found a pilot at Malindi who guided him across to India, opening the sea route from Europe.
